I found 17 problems across the three files. I judged them against the existing code (`customer_service.py`, `config.py`, `lib/apiClient.ts`, `lib/format.ts`, `OrderList.tsx`, `InvoiceList.tsx`).

## `app/api/loyalty_routes.py`

1. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py:1,10`** The route reads `LOYALTY_RATE` straight from `os.environ` on every request. Other settings live in `app/config.py`'s `Settings` and are loaded and checked once at startup. Here, a bad value like `LOYALTY_RATE=abc` only fails at request time, as a 500 on this one endpoint.
2. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py:11`** It calls `get_db().fetch_one(...)` directly instead of going through the service layer. It doesn't use `customer_service.get_customer` (the existing lookup), or even the `find_customer` defined in the new service.
3. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py:12-13`** A customer that doesn't exist returns `{"points": 0}` with a 200 status. That hides bad IDs and doesn't match `get_customer`, which raises `LookupError`. It should be a 404.
4. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py:14-15`** Points logic is split between the route and the service. The route doubles the rate for gold customers, and `points_for` also adds a +50 bonus for gold (`loyalty_service.py:16`). Gold customers get two bonuses, and no one reading only the service would know about the doubled rate. All tier rules belong in the service.

## `app/services/loyalty_service.py`

5. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:1`** `import json` is never used.
6. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:6-10`** `find_customer` is never called. Its `if row is None: return None` does nothing extra, since it returns `row` either way. It also repeats what `customer_service.get_customer` already does. Delete it.
7. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:13`** `points_for` takes a plain `dict` rather than the `Customer` model the rest of the services use. Several fields it reads aren't on `Customer`: `spent_cents`, `birthday_month`, `referrals`, `newsletter` and `blocked`. Either the model is missing them or the data shape isn't defined anywhere.
8. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:16-21,32`** The tier names `"gold"`, `"silver"` and `"bronze"` and the bonus amounts are hard-coded inline. A dict like `TIER_BONUS = {...}` would be clearer and keep the numbers in one place.
9. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:22-23`** Any truthy `birthday_month` adds 10 points, at any time of year. It almost certainly should check the month against the current month.
10. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:24-27`** `customer.get("referrals", 0)` is looked up twice. `20`, `25`, `5`, `3`, `1000` and the `> 3` threshold are unnamed magic numbers.
11. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:30-31`** The check for blocked customers runs after all the bonuses have been added. It should return 0 at the top of the function instead.
12. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:32-33`** Gold customers are exempt from the 1000-point cap. That's a third gold perk on top of the two in item 4. If it's intended, it needs a comment; if not, it's a bug.

## `web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx`

13. **`web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx:10`** A leftover `debugger;` statement sits in the render body. It pauses execution on every render whenever devtools are open. Remove it.
14. **`web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx:6-8`** The component calls `fetch` directly with a hard-coded `/api` prefix. The convention is `apiClient` from `lib/apiClient.ts`, wrapped in a typed function in `web/src/api/` (for example a `getLoyalty(id)` in a new `api/loyalty.ts`).
15. **`web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx:6-8`** There's no error handling. On a non-OK response, `body.points` is `undefined` and the badge shows "undefined pts"; a network failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. There's also no cleanup or cancellation, so if `customerId` changes quickly, an older response can overwrite a newer one.
16. **`web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx:4`** `points` starts at `0`, so the badge shows "0 pts" while loading. That can't be told apart from a real zero balance.
17. **`web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx:14-25`** `summarize` has nothing to do with loyalty badges. It's the third copy of the same function, after `OrderList.tsx:24` and `InvoiceList.tsx:24`. It also formats money with `(cents / 100).toFixed(2)` instead of the existing `formatCents` in `lib/format.ts`. Move one shared version into `lib/` and drop the copies.
